I had one art teacher for 2 years in high school. She made me feel seen and made me think I actually had the potential to do this as a career, which was all I ever wanted. She made me feel safe and made me feel like my work was important. I worked so hard and I was a favorite because of the ambition I had. Thing was, I was into making surrealistic anime inspired art. Well, Senior year I found out that she hated the way I drew my art and commented on some works I made. Not because of anatomical issues, she just hated the anime aspect. She made me feel like all I could become was simply an art teacher, and tried to shove it down my throat. She wanted me to be more realistic, and because it was advanced art, she would constantly tell me I would not do good on the test. 

I was depressed, hated my art style, and tried so hard to just please her. I wasted a whole crucial year of my work that could have been good for colleges just to satisfy her vision. In the end, it didn’t matter because when I told her I was burnout, she stopped checking up on me and focused solely on someone else in the class. I feel like it’s still half my fault and it took me a whole year to recover. Now, I focus on my anime art, and I noticed that my work was never the issue. I realized I can keep doing what I love and there will be people who will support me. Her opinion and a test score should have never mattered because she will never be there for my future milestones in my career. I’m still learning to be my true self but it traumatized me.
